strict.criterion: Ordinary see-through eyeglasses (and, in the 2010 restatement, contact lenses) directly project practical imagery onto the retina.
strict.rationale: Neither ordinary retinal-projection eyeglasses nor display contact lenses became practical products by 2009–2010 or by 2026. Microvision's 2004 Nomad was a bulky single-eye industrial headband deployed at auto dealerships, not ordinary see-through eyewear.
changedConditions: Enforces ordinary eyeglass/contact-lens form factor and practical deployment rather than a single industrial headset

evidence.note: Microvision-issued release hosted by The Auto Channel: actual industrial deployment. Head-worn see-through retinal display; not ordinary prescription-glasses styling or mass consumer adoption.

reference.criterion: Practical see-through eyeglass-form displays project imagery directly onto the retina for ordinary use, beyond isolated industrial prototypes.
reference.rationale: Microvision's 2004 Nomad deployment at a Chevrolet dealership proved direct retinal scanning could work in a head-worn unit before 2009, and later AR headsets pursued see-through displays. We do not count Nomad as full on-time fulfillment because a single bulky industrial headband falls well short of practical see-through eyeglass displays (and contact lenses from the 2010 restatement remain unrealized).

broader.criterion: Any working, commercially deployed see-through head-worn retinal display exists by 2009, regardless of industrial form factor or consumer adoption.
broader.rationale: Microvision's Nomad retinal display was commercially deployed for dealership mechanics in 2004, proving the core optical projection capability before 2009 if bulky industrial form factor and contact lenses are set aside.
